Question: Determine whether the following two code snippets are semantic code clones.

Code 1: Python
```python
a = int(input())
b = int(input())
print(a // b)
```

Code 2: Rust
```rust
use std::io;

fn read() -> i64 {
    let mut buf = String::new();
    io::stdin().read_line(&mut buf).unwrap();
    buf.trim().parse().unwrap()
}

fn main() {
    let a = read();
    let b = read();
    println!("{}", a / b);
}
```
<analysis>
Code 1 reads two integers and prints a // b, Python's floor division, which rounds toward negative infinity.<end_of_step>

Code 2 reads two integers and prints a / b, Rust integer division, which truncates toward zero.<end_of_step>

The two agree on non-negative inputs and differ only when the quotient is negative and inexact. That is invisible to inspection and to any test that only uses positive numbers, so run both sides on inputs that cross zero.<end_of_step>
<end_of_analysis>

<code>
import subprocess
<end_of_step>

def run_both(stdin_text):
    py = subprocess.run(["python3", "candidate_code.py"], input=stdin_text,
                        capture_output=True, text=True)
    rs = subprocess.run(["./candidate_code2"], input=stdin_text,
                        capture_output=True, text=True)
    return py.stdout.strip(), rs.stdout.strip()
<end_of_step>

# A negative, inexact quotient is where floor division and truncation split.
for case in ["7\n2", "-7\n2"]:
    out1, out2 = run_both(case)
    print(repr(case), "->", "Code 1:", out1, "| Code 2:", out2)
<end_of_code>
<output>
'7\n2' -> Code 1: 3 | Code 2: 3
'-7\n2' -> Code 1: -4 | Code 2: -3
Code 2 (Rust) compiled to ./candidate_code2: run it with subprocess.run(['./candidate_code2'], input=..., capture_output=True, text=True).
<end_of_output><answer>
Final decision: \boxed{non-clone}
Reason: Executed on the same inputs, Code 1 prints -4 where Code 2 prints -3: Python's // floors while Rust's / truncates, so the two programs do not compute the same function.
<end_of_answer>
